To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the resilience of social-ecological systems is determined by: (i) the degree to which the system is able to build and maintain the components that determine its structure, functioning, and identity; and (ii) the degree to Which the system is able, within a given range of conditions, to reorganize or restructure itself in order to maintain these components.
the resilience perspective provides a framework for understanding the dynamics and the sustainability of social-ecological systems.
the resilience of the system to the disturbance depends on the size of the disturbance and on the resilience of the ecosystem to the disturbance.
